findings.title: restoreControlValue reads owner-only r.node from native thread on Post failure
findings.message: When PostWindow fails, postControl runs restoreControlValue on the native event goroutine. That function reads r.node (Text, Number, SelectedID, Options) and mutates native widgets without the owner. r.node is owner-only state and may be rewritten by reconcile at the same time, so this is a data race. This diff widens the exposure: restoreControlValue now iterates r.node.Options for Chooser and Tabs. The new comment on requestControlRestore says owner state must not be touched without the proper lock.
findings.suggestion: On Post failure, do not read r.node off-owner. Mark the control for restore with an atomic flag and let the next owner-side sync apply it, or snapshot the restore values on the owner when the node is synced.

finding.title: Composer withdrawn after native resources are destroyed
finding.message: In native teardown the composer pointer is withdrawn only after Glw.Destroy() and Draw = nil. The patch intends Composer() and IsClosed() to be read without Mu. A lock-free caller can therefore still see a non-nil composer whose Drawer and Glw are already released or being destroyed, which defeats the withdrawal-before-teardown invariant stated in the comment.
finding.suggestion: Call w.composerPointer.Store(nil) at the start of the teardown, under Mu and before Glw.Destroy() and Draw release. Then every lock-free reader sees a closed window before any native resource is freed.

finding.title: Fixup silently skips all defaults when no screen is available
finding.message: NewWindowOptions.Fixup now returns early when no screen is available. This skips all remaining defaulting, including size, position and flags that do not depend on a screen. The previous code would have dereferenced nil here, so the early return hides the problem. Callers other than desktop NewWindow (which does check for nil) then receive half-initialized options, such as a zero size, without any error.
finding.suggestion: Fall back to a default screen geometry so Fixup still applies the other defaults, or have Fixup return an error that callers must handle. Do not silently skip the defaults.
